binders: p is a sequence indexed by natural numbers, with each p(n) a real number in the closed interval [0,1].
c and C are real constants.
hypotheses: For all sufficiently large natural numbers n, c ≤ (n-1)·p(n), where n-1 is computed in Nat and then cast to Real.
For all sufficiently large natural numbers n, (n-1)·p(n) ≤ C.
conclusions: For all sufficiently large n, under the binomial random graph law on simple graphs with vertex set Fin n and edge probability p(n), the real-valued measure of the event that some vertex v has degree at least (log n / log(log n)) / 128 is at least 9/10.
mathematical_definitions: The binomial random graph law independently includes each non-diagonal unordered pair of vertices as an edge with probability p(n).
The degree of a vertex is the cardinality of its neighbor set.
Eventually atTop on Nat means for every sufficiently large natural number.
The event is {G | there exists v in Fin n such that (log n / log(log n)) / 128 ≤ degree_G(v)}, with the natural degree cast to Real.
The probability-like quantity in the conclusion is Measure.real, namely the measure value converted from an extended nonnegative real to a real.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Let p(n) be edge probabilities in [0,1]. If the expected-degree scale (n-1)p(n) is eventually bounded below by a fixed positive constant c and eventually bounded above by a fixed real constant C, then for all sufficiently large n a binomial random graph on n vertices has, with probability at least 9/10, at least one vertex whose degree is at least log n divided by 128 times log(log n), equivalently (log n / log(log n)) / 128.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: All three asymptotic assertions use eventuality atTop on Nat, so they impose no requirements at finitely many small n.
The expression n-1 uses truncated natural subtraction before being cast to Real; this differs from first casting n to Real and subtracting 1 only at n=0.

Real.log is totalized and real division is totalized, so the displayed threshold is syntactically defined even when log n or log(log n) is zero or otherwise outside the usual positive-log regime; eventuality makes small-index behavior irrelevant to the intended asymptotic reading.
For n=0, Fin n has no vertices, so the existential graph event is empty, but this does not obstruct an eventual conclusion.

The assumptions are implications: for any particular p, c, and C for which an eventual bound fails, the corresponding implication is vacuously true. Moreover, the two eventual bounds together with c>0 force eventual compatibility c ≤ C whenever their antecedents are simultaneously satisfied.
The conclusion compares Measure.real with 9/10. Its probability interpretation relies on the binomialRandom measure being a finite probability measure, as supplied by its stated semantics.
The lower assumption only bounds (n-1)p(n) away from zero; it does not require this quantity to diverge. The upper assumption keeps it uniformly bounded for sufficiently large n.
The vertex degree is a natural number cast to Real before comparison with a generally nonintegral logarithmic threshold.
ambiguities: The phrase 'divided by 128 times log(log n)' can be linguistically ambiguous; the formal term is unambiguously left-associated as (log n / log(log n)) / 128 = log n / (128·log(log n)) whenever the usual nonzero-denominator algebra applies.

LocalDef004 is presented abstractly as an inductive type, but its constructor and projections make clear that the target uses its measure and degree-function fields; no further behavior of the package affects the proposition.

Measure.real converts an extended measure value to Real rather than being primitive probability notation, although for the stated binomial random graph probability measure it has the expected probability meaning.
